It has been a while since my last Avocado update.

It has been winter for the past while now, and I don't live in a hardiness zone where Avocados thrive so it hasnt been the most exciting times.

My avocado during the summer and even fall when it was sunny, had anywhere from 4-7 leaves at a time, and they all looked healthy and beautiful. Occasionally, one would get sunburned, or eaten and have to be replaced, but overall no big deal.

However, I have noticed a pattern lately.

My avocado will have about 2-3 leaves on it, they will look beautiful and fresh. His water regiment stays the same. Within about 1 week parts on one of the leaves will start to gray or brown, and the leaf will die, then slowly the next one, and even more slowly the next one.

Soon he will have no leaves, then about 1 week later he will start to grow again and put out spots where 3-4 leaves are going to turn out.

Repeat process, again and again and again.

Now, I don't know much about plant biology and stuff like that, so I have made an uneducated hypothesis, tell me what you guys think.

I believe that with the current amount of sunlight he is receiving, when he has no leaves or extra body to support he believes he can grow. So, he puts out 3-4 new leaves, once the leaves develop and he now has to support these children the little amount of sunlight he gets is not enough, so they die, and then he thinks he can grow again due to now being free and having no children. Repeat cycle.

Let me know what you guys think.

Thanks.

From what I understand, every avocado you find (at least in stores of the western world) is a Hass avocado.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hass_avocado

Virtually all production avocados are grafts of this original tree from the 1920's. Avocados, like apples will generate various forms of the original parents, which may or may not grow to maturity or even produce edible fruit. This is the reasoning for grafting.

With this said, I have started 3 avocado's so far. 2 ended up getting caught in cold frost before bringing inside and we lost them. The 3rd is in its 3'rd year now. about 30" tall. Fingers crossed. Only 5+? years to go to see if/what fruit might be like....
